overall_reason: A provides the stronger appointment-booking composition: its restrained heading treatment, earlier access to the booking controls on mobile, and compact supporting sections make the required task easier to find and scan. B has a more consistent repeated section-heading pattern, but its additional heading layers, copy, and service section lengthen the page without a corresponding improvement in the primary booking hierarchy. This preference concerns the visible designs only. Observations: pair-001: A places the booking card at about y=528, with the day choices visible around y=726; B starts its booking card around y=709, so the initial 844px viewport reaches only the service selector. Both retain three day and three time buttons in the mobile column. pair-002: A moves from the two booking cards directly into the three steps, two FAQ rows, and a simple footer within a 1468px page. B adds a separate service-description section and larger inter-section gaps, producing a 2010px page. pair-001 and pair-002: A keeps the large hero headline navy and reserves the strongest filled blue treatment for action buttons. B adds a large bright-blue headline phrase and repeated uppercase blue section labels, increasing the number of competing emphases.

criteria.reason: The visible required product content is substantially present in both: the specified header on desktop, exact hero headline and description, primary CTA, booking and preview cards, three steps, two FAQ topics, and footer. Neither default still establishes the required updates, post-preview notice, navigation behavior, focus treatment, or reduced-motion behavior, so there is no supported overall compliance winner. Observations: pair-002: Both headers show Morrow, Features, Specialists, How it works, Sign in, and Book a session; both hero areas show the requested headline, description, and Find a session CTA. pair-001 and pair-002: Both show Consultation selected, Monday/Tuesday/Wednesday choices, 09:00/11:30/14:00 choices, and a neighboring or stacked preview showing Consultation, Monday, and 09:00. pair-001 and pair-002: Both show the three requested step titles, FAQ questions about rescheduling and real booking, and a footer. B additionally exposes one demo explanation in an expanded FAQ; A shows both FAQ rows collapsed.

A gives the primary booking task a more direct reading order, especially on mobile. Its navy hero and concise transition into the controls leave the blue action buttons as the clearest emphases. B remains understandable, but its large blue headline phrase and extra booking-section heading create more visual stops before the form. Observations: pair-001: A follows its left-aligned headline and description with Find a session, then a short one-line introduction and the booking card. B follows its centered hero with a CTA, a helper line, an uppercase eyebrow, a two-line section heading, and another sentence before its card. pair-002: A uses a small A little time, just for you line above the cards; B inserts MAKE A LITTLE ROOM FOR YOU and the large A good time starts here heading between hero and controls. pair-001 and pair-002: A uses navy for the entire hero headline; B makes beautifully simple a large blue focal area in addition to the blue primary and preview buttons.

Both use clear sans-serif type, strong navy headings, readable warm card surfaces, and intact control labels. B has darker and heavier form labels and a more compact two-line desktop headline; A has fewer small auxiliary labels and shorter supporting copy. Neither has a decisive overall readability advantage in the supplied views. Observations: pair-002: B wraps the headline into two lines while A uses three; both headings remain legible and visually separate from their descriptions. pair-001: Both mobile headlines wrap without clipping, and Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and all three time labels fit inside their individual buttons. pair-001 and pair-002: B makes its form labels and unselected choice labels heavier, while A reduces the number of uppercase micro-labels and supplementary sentences. Both distinguish headings, body copy, and field labels clearly.

A has the more effective content density and section pacing. Its aligned card pair and concise lower page form a complete, intentional composition, while B devotes more vertical space to repeated introductory copy, expanded supporting content, and large gaps between sections. Observations: pair-002: A aligns both booking cards from approximately y=484 to y=856, then starts the steps heading around y=922. Its FAQ and footer complete the page by y=1468. pair-002: B also aligns its two cards well, but the steps, separate Different needs service section, FAQ, and footer stretch the composition to y=2010, with pronounced open space between the steps and service section. pair-001: A keeps hero, card stack, steps, FAQ, and footer aligned to a 20px outer gutter and completes the page at 2188px. B shifts from a centered hero to left-aligned sections and extends to 3003px with more introductory and supporting material.

B applies its repeated visual patterns more systematically across the full page. Its uppercase blue section eyebrows, bold section headings, numbered pale-blue circles, and choice-label weights form a particularly consistent set. A is coherent, but its booking introduction and later section introductions follow more varied patterns. Observations: pair-002: B repeats an uppercase blue eyebrow over the booking, steps, service, and FAQ headings; A uses a hero eyebrow, a small single-line booking introduction, and later headings with separate subtitle arrangements. pair-001 and pair-002: B repeats the same pale-blue circular number treatment for all three steps and consistently bold day/time button labels, including unselected choices. pair-001 and pair-002: Both repeat their logo, rounded warm cards, blue buttons, and thin separators coherently; B has the additional advantage of a regular section-title pattern through its longer page.

Both successfully show a desktop card pair and a usable-looking mobile stack without visible horizontal clipping. A adapts the task priorities more effectively to the narrow view by reaching the controls earlier, keeping a common left edge, and reducing the amount of supporting material a mobile reader must pass. Observations: pair-001: A starts the booking card around y=528 and exposes the day row in the first viewport; B starts it around y=709 and places the day/time rows below the initial viewport. pair-001 and pair-002: Both change the adjacent desktop cards into a single mobile column, and both preserve all three day and time buttons across the available card width without visible overflow. pair-001: A keeps the hero and subsequent section headings left-aligned to the same page gutter. B centers the hero but switches to left alignment for the longer booking and supporting sections.

Both coherently adapt the reference principles rather than reproducing its content: bold sans-serif heading hierarchy, a cool light page, warm lightly textured card surfaces, restrained rounded borders, and blue controls. A stays closer to the reference navy headline treatment; B makes a more expressive blue headline treatment while preserving the same card-versus-page distinction. Neither is a clear winner on the requested principles alone. Observations: pair-002 versus assets/reference-001.png: Both alternatives retain the reference large heading above two neighboring warm pale cards, with fine cool borders, rounded corners, and bright blue action controls. pair-001 versus assets/reference-002.png: Both preserve the reference mobile principle of a single column with generous outer gutters and stacked rounded cards while expanding the controls for the target product. pair-002: A retains an entirely navy hero heading; B uses navy plus a blue emphasized phrase. Both maintain an obvious hierarchy between hero text, card headings, labels, and supporting copy.

limitations: Only the supplied default-state screenshots at 390px and 1440px widths were assessed; no implementation files, interactions, or other states were inspected.

Still images do not establish CTA destinations, selector options hidden by the closed dropdown, selection updates, preview status behavior, menu opening or closing, keyboard focus, semantic accessibility, or reduced-motion support.
The required exact post-preview sentence is not visible in either default view; this does not establish whether it appears after activation.
Apparent readability and the absence of visible clipping do not establish measured color-contrast compliance or complete accessibility.
This comparison assesses these two visible alternatives and does not establish a general improvement in design skill.
